symptom: Host CPU usage spikes from kvm-pit kernel threads but the cost isn't accounted to any microVM cgroup. Schedulers undercount per-tenant CPU; noisy-neighbor effects.

diagnostic_steps.command: for tid in $(ps -L -o tid= -p <fc-pid>); do cat /proc/$tid/cgroup; done
diagnostic_steps.expected: kvm-pit threads in root cgroup, not microVM cgroup

fix_steps.action: Run an external agent that moves kvm-pit threads into the microVM's cgroup post-start
fix_steps.command: After Firecracker starts, find kvm-pit/<fc-pid> tids and write them to <microvm-cgroup>/cgroup.procs (v2) or tasks (v1)
fix_steps.validation: kvm-pit CPU now accounted to the microVM
fix_steps.rollback: Move them back to root cgroup

fix_steps.action: Or raise the kvm timer-period limit to reduce kvm-pit work
fix_steps.command: sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel kvm; sudo modprobe kvm min_timer_period_us=1000; sudo modprobe kvm_intel; persist via /etc/modprobe.d/kvm.conf
fix_steps.validation: kvm-pit CPU drops; APIC granularity coarsens (workload-test)

symptom: Snapshot restore time degrades inexplicably (e.g., 3ms → 8.5ms on aarch64) after host kernel cmdline change. Host kernel logging hot during TAP create — synchronous console writes hold up the FC main thread.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should contain `quiet loglevel=1`; any console=ttyAMA0 / console=ttyS0 is suspect

diagnostic_steps.action: Check dmesg log volume during restore
diagnostic_steps.expected: Few lines if quiet loglevel=1 is set

fix_steps.action: Add quiet loglevel=1 to host kernel cmdline; remove any console= entries
fix_steps.command: Edit /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX; update-grub; reboot

symptom: Multi-tenant Firecracker host has SMT (Hyperthreading) enabled. Speculation-class side channels (Spectre, MDS) become exploitable across tenants.

fix_steps.action: Disable SMT at runtime
fix_steps.command: echo off | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/smt/control
fix_steps.validation: smt/control shows off; lscpu Thread(s) per core = 1

fix_steps.action: Make persistent: add nosmt to host kernel cmdline
fix_steps.command: Edit /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX; update-grub; reboot

symptom: Multi-tenant host has KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging) enabled. Page-deduplication side channels exploitable — one tenant can detect another's memory contents.

fix_steps.action: Disable KSM and unmerge
fix_steps.command: echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run

fix_steps.action: Make persistent via systemd unit
fix_steps.command: Add a systemd unit that sets ksm/run=0 at boot; or set kernel.ksm_run=0 sysctl if your distro maps it

symptom: Host has swap enabled. Under memory pressure, guest memory contents get written to disk → data remanence on disk reuse.

fix_steps.action: Disable all swap
fix_steps.command: sudo swapoff -a; remove swap entries from /etc/fstab

fix_steps.action: If swap is required, use encrypted swap (LUKS over swap partition)
fix_steps.command: Configure dm-crypt-managed swap
fix_steps.validation: Swap pages are encrypted at rest

symptom: Firecracker fails with EMFILE (Too many open files) when starting many devices or under vsock-heavy workload. Each microVM uses 20+ FDs baseline.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Soft limit ≥ 4096 for moderate workloads, much higher for vsock-heavy

fix_steps.action: Raise via jailer --resource-limit
fix_steps.command: jailer ... --resource-limit no-file=8192 ...
fix_steps.validation: Limits file shows new limit; Firecracker doesn't hit EMFILE

fix_steps.action: Or systemd unit LimitNOFILE
fix_steps.command: Set [Service] LimitNOFILE=8192 in unit file; systemctl daemon-reload; restart

symptom: Production Firecracker is started with --no-seccomp (or with a custom filter that whitelists too many syscalls). Defense-in-depth boundary disabled.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should NOT include --no-seccomp; --seccomp-filter only when needed

fix_steps.action: Remove --no-seccomp from launch script
fix_steps.command: Update orchestrator/systemd unit to drop the flag

fix_steps.action: If a custom filter is needed, audit it; only whitelist what's strictly required
fix_steps.command: Review the JSON; remove unnecessary syscall allowances; recompile via seccompiler-bin

symptom: Production deployment is using a debug-built Firecracker binary. Default seccomp filters are not embedded in debug builds — process runs unsandboxed at the syscall layer.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check Seccomp status as a confirmation
diagnostic_steps.expected: Seccomp: 2; if 0 with no --no-seccomp → likely debug build

fix_steps.action: Replace with release build (musl static)
fix_steps.command: Pull official release tarball or rebuild with --release

symptom: Host crashes; on reboot, guest filesystem is corrupted or 'recently committed' data is missing. Drive was attached with cache_type=Unsafe — guest fsync()s were dropped.

diagnostic_steps.expected: 'Writeback' for any drive holding non-ephemeral data

fix_steps.action: Restart microVM with cache_type=Writeback for persistent drives
fix_steps.command: Pre-boot: PUT /drives/<id> {..., cache_type: 'Writeback'}

symptom: PUT /drives returns 400 with 'Block device backing file does not exist' or InstanceStart fails reading the disk.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check the configured path_on_host (resolved relative to chroot if jailed)
diagnostic_steps.expected: File exists and is readable by the FC uid

fix_steps.action: Copy/bind-mount the backing file into the chroot before PUT /drives
fix_steps.command: Inside jail setup: cp <host-path> <chroot>/<inside-path>; chown <fc-uid>

fix_steps.action: Or pass the file via --bind-mount in your jailer setup script
fix_steps.command: Use a wrapper that mounts the host path into the chroot read-only or read-write
fix_steps.validation: FC sees file at the configured chroot-relative path

symptom: API call returns 400 with 'cannot be modified after machine startup' or similar. Trying to PUT a pre-boot-only resource (drive, network-interface, vsock, machine-config, boot-source, mmds-config) after InstanceStart.
error_patterns: cannot be modified after machine startup

diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'Running' or 'Paused' → pre-boot resources are immutable

fix_steps.action: Snapshot, destroy, restart fresh microVM with the new pre-boot config
fix_steps.command: PATCH /vm{Paused}; PUT /snapshot/create; SIGKILL; new FC process; load snapshot OR fresh boot with new config
fix_steps.validation: Resource takes effect on the new microVM

fix_steps.action: If only the rate limiter or drive backing file needs changing, use PATCH (those ARE runtime-mutable)
fix_steps.command: PATCH /drives/<id> {path_on_host: <new>} OR PATCH /network-interfaces/<id> {tx_rate_limiter: <new>}

symptom: Jailer fails with 'no internal process constraint' when launched with --cgroup-version=2 + --parent-cgroup pointing at an existing cgroup that has domain controllers in subtree_control.

fix_steps.action: Move the jailer to a leaf cgroup (no subtree_control set)
fix_steps.command: Use a different --parent-cgroup that's a leaf, or pass --cgroup args so jailer creates its own subdir

fix_steps.action: Or remove domain controllers from subtree_control
fix_steps.command: echo '-memory -cpu' | sudo tee /sys/fs/cgroup/<parent>/cgroup.subtree_control
fix_steps.validation: Parent now empty; jailer move succeeds

symptom: Jailer exits with EACCES creating <chroot_base>/<exec>/<id>/root. The chroot base directory or its parents have wrong permissions.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check chroot-base-dir permissions all the way down
diagnostic_steps.expected: Path is writable by the user invoking jailer (typically root)

fix_steps.action: Pre-create with correct perms
fix_steps.command: sudo mkdir -p /srv/jailer; sudo chmod 755 /srv/jailer
fix_steps.validation: Jailer creates the chroot tree successfully

fix_steps.action: Ensure paths aren't writable by unprivileged users (per the prod-host-setup recommendation)
fix_steps.command: sudo chmod 700 /srv/jailer; sudo chown root:root /srv/jailer

symptom: MicroVM with VirtIO balloon overcommitted memory thrashes — guest's effective RAM drops to a tiny fraction (e.g., 8 GiB → 1.4 GiB) causing massive page churn.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check balloon size vs guest available memory
diagnostic_steps.expected: amount_mib should leave guest enough free memory for working set
swap_in / swap_out trending up indicates pressure

fix_steps.action: Deflate the balloon to give the guest memory back
fix_steps.command: PATCH /balloon {amount_mib: <smaller>}
fix_steps.validation: Guest free memory recovers; swap rate drops

fix_steps.action: Set deflate_on_oom=true so balloon auto-deflates under guest OOM pressure
fix_steps.command: PUT /balloon {amount_mib: 0, deflate_on_oom: true, stats_polling_interval_s: 5} (pre-boot only, requires VM restart)

symptom: Orchestrator (e2b-style) tries to kill a Firecracker process while UFFD handler is mid-fault-service. Process kill races with handler cleanup → orphaned UFFD state, leaked fds, hung handlers.

diagnostic_steps.command: ps aux | grep uffd-handler; lsof | grep userfaultfd
diagnostic_steps.expected: Zero handlers without a paired Firecracker

fix_steps.action: Sequence kills: SIGTERM Firecracker first, wait for vCPU thread exit, then signal UFFD handler
fix_steps.command: kill -TERM <fc-pid>; wait $fc; kill -TERM <uffd-pid>
fix_steps.rollback: Use SIGKILL on both (current racy behavior)

fix_steps.action: Track e2b-dev/infra PR #148 for the canonical lifecycle fix
fix_steps.command: Monitor github.com/e2b-dev/infra/pull/148

symptom: Orchestrator (e2b-style) client process restarts → all live Firecracker sandboxes crash. UFFD handler closure on client exit cascades to FCs that depend on it.

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace the failure chain — which process closure killed which sandboxes
diagnostic_steps.command: Add audit logging on UFFD handler exit → FC death

fix_steps.action: Decouple UFFD handler lifecycle from client process — run it as a separate long-lived service
fix_steps.command: Architectural: standalone uffd-server process, client only registers FCs with it

fix_steps.action: Or implement UFFD handler reattachment on restart
fix_steps.command: Persist per-FC UFFD state to disk; new handler instance reads on startup
fix_steps.validation: Handler crash + restart leaves FCs running

symptom: Guest clock drifts by ~100-500ms on startup. KVM PTP not configured in guest; guest relies on its initial RTC read which lags.

fix_steps.action: Build guest kernel with CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK=y and CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM=y; configure chrony to use /dev/ptp0
fix_steps.command: Edit kernel config; rebuild; in guest: add 'refclock PHC /dev/ptp0 poll 3 dpoll -2 offset 0' to /etc/chrony/chrony.conf; restart chrony
fix_steps.validation: guest$ chronyc tracking shows /dev/ptp0 source; drift <1ms

symptom: Orchestrator-level health-check failure (Nomad/Consul) triggers a cascade of Firecracker process restarts. The actual fault wasn't with FC.

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify trigger — orchestrator log around the cascade time
Differentiate FC fault vs orchestrator fault
diagnostic_steps.command: Per-FC log inspection during the same window
diagnostic_steps.expected: FCs were healthy when orchestrator killed them

fix_steps.action: Tune orchestrator health-check thresholds — allow brief blips
fix_steps.command: Raise Nomad check_restart.limit; widen health-check interval

fix_steps.action: Decouple FC lifecycle from orchestrator restart
fix_steps.command: Use a separate FC supervisor that doesn't restart on orchestrator-level events
fix_steps.validation: Orchestrator can restart independently of FC fleet

symptom: VirtIO/net TX throughput is lower than expected. Packets get copied twice — descriptor → intermediate buffer → kernel — instead of using scatter-gather.

diagnostic_steps.action: Compare against Firecracker version where scatter-gather was added (PR #2958)
diagnostic_steps.command: firecracker --version; check CHANGELOG for scatter-gather mention

fix_steps.action: Upgrade Firecracker to a version >= the PR #2958 release
fix_steps.command: Update binary

symptom: VM with track_dirty_pages=true sees noticeable per-write overhead (small but measurable on write-heavy workloads). KVM page-walk for dirty bits adds cost.

diagnostic_steps.action: Benchmark write throughput with and without
diagnostic_steps.command: Run fio random-write workload pre and post

fix_steps.action: If diff snapshots aren't needed, disable track_dirty_pages
fix_steps.command: Pre-boot: PUT /machine-config {..., track_dirty_pages: false}; restart VM

fix_steps.action: If keeping diff snapshots, accept the trade-off — it's by design

symptom: PUT /machine-config with huge_pages='2M' fails or microVM creates fail under load. Host hasn't reserved enough hugepages.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Reserved >= sum of expected microVM RAM in 2M units

fix_steps.action: Reserve hugepages before starting microVMs
fix_steps.command: echo <N> | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages

fix_steps.action: Persist via sysctl
fix_steps.command: echo 'vm.nr_hugepages=<N>' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/hugepages.conf

symptom: machine-config.smt is true on a multi-tenant host. Guest sees hyperthreaded siblings via CPUID — speculation side-channel attack surface increases.

fix_steps.action: Set smt=false (pre-boot only, requires VM restart)
fix_steps.command: PUT /machine-config {..., smt: false}; restart VM
fix_steps.validation: guest$ lscpu shows Thread(s) per core: 1

symptom: Operator attempts to bind the Firecracker API to a TCP port. Firecracker only accepts UDS transport.

fix_steps.action: Use UDS; bridge to TCP via socat or similar if remote access needed
fix_steps.command: socat TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/firecracker.socket
fix_steps.validation: TCP clients can reach the API; security: protect with firewall + auth proxy

fix_steps.action: For multi-host orchestration, use a per-host control plane that holds UDS local and exposes its own auth'd API
fix_steps.command: Architectural — orchestrator owns the UDS, exposes a tenant-isolated REST/gRPC

symptom: PUT /actions {action_type: InstanceStart} returns 400. Required pre-boot resources aren't all configured.

fix_steps.action: Configure each missing resource before InstanceStart
fix_steps.command: PUT /boot-source; PUT /machine-config; PUT /drives/<id> with is_root_device=true; (optional: /network-interfaces, /vsock, etc.); THEN PUT /actions
